record.title: PSD reports transferring black-box memory construction into small Qwen models
record.summary: A September 20 preprint introduces pseudo self-distillation (PSD), which uses outputs from a closed-model oracle as prompt context for a Qwen model acting as a privileged teacher, then trains a student to match its output distribution without access to teacher logits or hidden states. In the authors’ LoCoMo test, a PSD-trained Qwen3-4B receives an overall LLM-judge score of 0.8699 versus 0.849 for the original MEMORA pipeline using GPT-4.1-mini; the paper also reports improvements over its own SFT checkpoint at all three tested Qwen sizes. These are author-reported results. The reported score comparison does not establish total training-plus-inference cost savings.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On the full LoCoMo benchmark test split, the authors report an overall LLM-judge score of 0.8699 for PSD-trained Qwen3-4B, compared with 0.849 for MEMORA using GPT-4.1-mini. The paper reports that the PSD stage improves over SFT at all three tested Qwen3 sizes; these are author-run results, not independent reproductions.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For LongMemEval, the authors evaluate on a category-balanced 100-question subset of the 500-question benchmark. Qwen3-4B PSD scores 0.77 on this subset, while the paper’s Full Context and Nemori references are 0.656 and 0.746 on the full benchmark; the different evaluation denominators limit direct comparison. The within-paper Base/SFT/PSD checkpoints use the same subset.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reported benchmark results do not establish lower total cost than repeated GPT-4.1-mini memory construction, because oracle-data generation, fine-tuning and student inference costs are not compared under a matched workload.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of LoCoMo or LongMemEval results was located or performed.
Total teacher-data generation, fine-tuning and student inference costs are not compared against repeated GPT-4.1-mini memory construction under the same workload.
The LongMemEval PSD result is measured on a 100-question subset while cited Full Context and Nemori results use the full benchmark.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported transfer holds, the method could make structured long-horizon memory construction practical with smaller models. Its broader economic consequence remains uncertain because the paper does not compare training, oracle-data generation and inference costs end to end.
limitations: The numerical results are reported by the authors and were not independently reproduced.
The primary outcome is an LLM-judge score using GPT-4o-mini; no human-judged replication or judge-sensitivity analysis was performed here.
LongMemEval’s PSD result uses a 100-question subset, whereas the cited Full Context and Nemori values use the full benchmark.
The paper does not measure end-to-end economics including oracle-data generation, fine-tuning and student inference under a matched workload.
brief.summary: A September 20 preprint introduces pseudo self-distillation (PSD), which uses outputs from a closed-model oracle as prompt context for a Qwen model acting as a privileged teacher, then trains a student to match its output distribution without access to teacher logits or hidden states. In the authors’ LoCoMo test, a PSD-trained Qwen3-4B receives an overall LLM-judge score of 0.8699 versus 0.849 for the original MEMORA pipeline using GPT-4.1-mini; the paper also reports improvements over its own SFT checkpoint at all three tested Qwen sizes. These are author-reported results. The reported score comparison does not establish total training-plus-inference cost savings.

technical.claimed_result: On LoCoMo, the authors report a 0.8699 overall LLM-judge score for PSD-trained Qwen3-4B versus 0.849 for MEMORA with GPT-4.1-mini; the reported PSD stage raises scores over SFT from 0.7805 to 0.8699 at 4B, 0.7805 to 0.8211 at 1.7B, and 0.7674 to 0.8211 at 0.6B. On a 100-question LongMemEval subset, Qwen3-4B PSD scores 0.77, but full-benchmark baseline comparisons use a different denominator.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected preprint documents the method and author-reported benchmark values. the research desk did not run the code or independently reproduce the results.
technical.mechanism: A closed-model oracle generates stage-labeled answers for LoCoMo training conversations. A Qwen model receives the oracle answer as privileged reference context in a teacher role; the same model in a student role receives only the task prompt. Training first uses supervised fine-tuning, then minimizes divergence between teacher and student output distributions using either oracle-anchored off-policy or student-rollout on-policy examples.
technical.regime: Qwen3-0.6B, 1.7B and 4B students are trained on LoCoMo with a 50:50 train/test split and evaluated on its held-out test set. GPT-4.1-mini provides oracle answers for training; GPT-4o-mini is the LLM judge. LongMemEval is not used for training; the authors evaluate a category-balanced 100-question subset of its 500 questions. Table 2 compares LoCoMo with the full MEMORA and prior-system results.
technical.strongest_baseline: For the reported overall LoCoMo LLM-judge score, MEMORA with GPT-4.1-mini is 0.849 versus 0.8699 for PSD-trained Qwen3-4B. BLEU and F1 still favor some full-context and larger-backbone systems. LongMemEval baselines are evaluated on all 500 questions while the PSD model uses a 100-question subset, so those cross-system values are not matched.

brief.title: PSD reports transferring black-box memory construction into small Qwen models
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported performance generalizes, black-box distillation may transfer structured memory-construction behavior into smaller models where direct prompting performs poorly. That could change deployment choices for persistent agent memory, but the paper does not compare total oracle generation, fine-tuning and student inference cost with repeated calls to the larger model; its LongMemEval comparison also uses a 100-question subset against baselines evaluated on the full set.
